headlines.title: Woman will plead not guilty in killing of son-in-law at Dublin park, attorney says
headlines.description: The attorney for a Dublin woman who was charged along with her husband in the killing of their son-in-law said Thursday that she plans to plead not guilty and focus her defense on the abuse allegedly perpetrated by the victim. Shili Chen and her husband Shouyong Zhang, both 77, appeared in court briefly to ask the judge for more time before entering formal pleas. They were both charged Wednesday with murder after authorities say they both shot their son-in-law, Jonathan McKinsey, to death Saturday in a public park. The killing came days before he and the couple’s daughter were set for a hearing in a bitter divorce and custody case. Curtis Briggs, a court-appointed attorney assigned Thursday to Chen’s defense, said the court documents he has reviewed raised concerns that McKinsey was rageful and could not control his temper. “Court documents show Mr. McKinsey was extremely violent and dangerous to his family,” he said. Jennie Otis, a public defender representing Zhang, asked the judge on Thursday that he be medically evaluated, though she did not say for what. Otis declined to comment. Both required Mandarin interpreters in the courtroom. Dublin Sep 30 Dublin Sep 29 Dublin Sep 27 McKinsey, a 40-year-old gaming engineer for The New York Times, was killed in the parking lot of a sports complex in Dublin. A police sergeant was driving nearby and saw him on the ground as witnesses began calling 911 and pointing out the couple in their vehicle, who were still near the scene, Dublin Police Services said in a news release. Police detained the couple as they were driving away in the parking lot and found a gun in Chen’s possession. Prosecutors said Zhang admitted to shooting McKinsey during a later interview, and another firearm was found in the car that he admitted to using during the crime. Prosecutors also said surveillance video was recovered showing both Chen and Zhang shooting the victim. Court records show McKinsey’s killing came during a contentious divorce with his wife, Candice Jang, and a custody battle over the couple’s three young children. In petitions for restraining orders filed last year, the couple accused each other of physical, emotional and psychological abuse going back more than a decade. McKinsey, who is transgender, alleged that both Jang and her parents were verbally and physically abusive regarding a gender transition he underwent years ago. McKinsey was arrested last October and charged with misdemeanor child abuse for allegedly hitting their oldest son. Police said he acknowledged having slapped the child. Prosecutors also charged him with endangering their youngest child after deputies responded to the family’s home to talk with him and found their 2-year-old had been left home alone, according to court documents. McKinsey pleaded not guilty to the charges and alleged in court records that he had been set up by his wife, who had left the house without telling him the child was sleeping in a crib upstairs. He was released from jail on the condition that he complete 12 parenting classes. At the time of his killing, McKinsey was out on bail and had been trying to enter a mental health diversion program. It was also in October that Jang obtained a domestic violence protection order against McKinsey. Jang wrote a long list of alleged abuse by McKinsey in her filing, including an instance in 2010 when McKinsey allegedly had grabbed her by the forearms during an argument and caused her to hit the corner of a coffee table, fracturing a vertebra in her upper back. She also said that in 2023 she called the police to their home after McKinsey pushed their oldest son hard on the head. Jang also accused McKinsey of emotionally abusing her mother. The Associated Press has been unable to reach Jang for comment.

headlines.title: Pedestrian killed in Castro Valley hit-and-run collision
headlines.description: A pedestrian was fatally struck during a hit-and-run collision in Castro Valley. The incident was reported 1:29 p.m. Thursday near Somerset and Anita avenues in a residential area near Our Lady of Grace Catholic School, according to the California Highway Patrol. Alameda County Sheriff’s Office deputies have also responded with the CHP to investigate the incident. CHP said the pedestrian, a 50-year-old man, was in the roadway when struck. Police are searching for the driver and suspect vehicle. A description of the suspect was not immediately available.

headlines.title: Manny Yekutiel suspends San Francisco District 8 supervisor bid
headlines.description: San Francisco business owner Manny Yekutiel announced Thursday he is suspending his campaign for District 8 supervisor. The decision comes after the San Francisco Standard reported sexual assault allegations against Yekutiel. Supervisor Connie Chan prior to Yekutiel suspending his campaign also called for him to step down. “After a great deal of reflection, I have made the difficult decision to end my campaign for District 8 supervisor,” Yekutiel said. “I am not admitting to having assaulted anyone and some of the things that are being said about me are fundamentally untrue. But I am deeply sorry for any boundaries that I crossed. I’m going to take this time to work on myself.” Here’s the rest of Yekutiel’s statement: “As I said from the very beginning, I’m not a typical candidate. Moving through the machinery of San Francisco’s politics has left me with very little light left in my heart. This campaign has meant more to me than I can put into words. Over the past months, I have had the privilege of talking with thousands of San Franciscans about the city we love, the challenges we face, and the future we want to build together. This was never just about winning an election for me. It was about serving a city that has given me so much and bringing people together around the belief that San Francisco can once again take on big challenges with ambition, creativity, and confidence.I am incredibly proud of the campaign we built and of the community that formed around it. I am especially grateful to all of the block captains, house party hosts, family, friends, staff, volunteers, supporters, and everyone who stood with me. My campaign may be ending, but my work to help build a better San Francisco has only just begun.”

headlines.title: Bay Area weather forecast: Weekend heat advisory issued
headlines.description: The calendar has flipped to October, but the Bay Area will face summer-like heat this weekend. The National Weather Service has issued a heat advisory for much of the region beginning at 11 a.m. Saturday and lasting until 10 p.m. Sunday. Inland locations could see high temperatures peaking anywhere from the mid-90s to low 100s, according to the weather service. The public is encouraged to shift outdoor plans to cooler times of the day. Those who have to be outside during the hottest hours should take frequent breaks in air conditioning or shade and drink plenty of water. Watch the latest Bay Area weather forecast in the video player above. This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.

headlines.title: Built on grit: Jim Plunkett's Bay Area journey to becoming an NFL legend
headlines.description: Football legend Jim Plunkett came from humble beginnings in East San Jose before rising to the top of the NFL. During his professional football career, Plunkett was named Rookie of the Year, Most Valuable Player, and also won a Super Bowl playing quarterback for the Raiders. In this Hispanic Heritage Month spotlight, Damian Trujillo shares how Plunkett’s grit overcame a tough upbringing to become a sports legend. comunidad del valle May 4 Sep 22 Hispanic Heritage Month Sep 21 Hispanic Heritage Month spotlight: Con Azucar Café owner Alejandra Gonzalez

headlines.title: No longer a secret, Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes doc ‘You Can See Everything' lands in New York
headlines.description: No longer a secret, “You Can See Everything,” Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary, premiered Wednesday at the New York Film Festival. Since first debuting in a surprise, no-phones screening at the Telluride Film Festival on Sept. 6, “You Can See Everything” immediately transformed into one of the year’s most buzzed-about films. Shot secretly over three years, the nearly three-hour documentary captures Holmes, founder of the medical testing company Theranos, in the 34 days before reporting to prison. But as fans of Fielder would expect, little in how “You Can See Everything” follows a conventional route. Moviegoers lined up outside the Alice Tully Hall at Lincoln Center as early as 3 a.m. in hopes of attending the sold-out 8 p.m. screening. “You Can See Everything,” which A24 will release Oct. 16, is a hard-to-believe coda to a preposterous saga. Even Fielder isn’t sure what to make of the surreal odyssey he and Oppenheim captured. “I am still struggling to this day to understand what I went through,” Fielder said in a Q&A following the screening. Crime and Courts Sep 24 Movies Sep 7 After her conviction on four felony counts of fraud and conspiracy, Holmes entered a Texas prison in May 2023. In a headline-grabbing scandal that rocked Silicon Valley, one of the most surprising and surreal twists was revealed only this month. Holmes chose to let Fielder, the absurdist comedian of “Nathan For You” and “The Rehearsal,” and the documentary filmmaker Oppenheim, intimately film her life with her partner, the California hotel heir Billy Evans, and their two children. At this dramatic moment in their lives, Fielder lived in a guest house at their Del Mar, California, beachside home. The filmmakers shot from morning to night. Fielder interviews the couple while in bed, or the bathroom. “I mean, I cannot tell you how weird it was that we were there,” Fielder said. “I wouldn’t think I’d be, like, the person that you would want for your final 34 days of freedom. I’m not the most, like, comforting.” The filmmakers happened to hear that Holmes and Evans had reached out to A24 about the prospect of making a documentary. Fielder didn’t initially think it would amount to a feature film, but he was curious just to meet Holmes. “When I met her, I remember having this weird experience,” Fielder explained. “She seems so genuine at times but then I’m like, (expletive), tracking my thoughts and being like, ‘I know she’s a liar.’” “Every person who worked on this movie was going through a similar cognitive dissonance,” said Oppenheim, who directed the just-released “Primetime,” starring Robert Pattinson as “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen. “We would unpack the day’s events and no one could agree on seemingly mundane moments that would transpire.” In “You Can See Everything,” Fielder seeks not only to grasp what is true and not true about Holmes, but to grapple with deeper questions of identity, performance, fiction and control. Holmes founded Theranos with her then-romantic partner Ramesh “Sunny” Balwani. They promised the company would revolutionize healthcare with a technology that could quickly scan for diseases and other health problems with a few drops of blood taken with a finger prick. The hype helped them raise nearly $1 billion from investors. By 2014, Theranos was valued at $4.5 billion. But after the company’s purported technology advances were exposed in a series of explosive articles in The Wall Street Journal, the company collapsed. In 2018, the U.S. Justice Department charged Holmes and Balwani with a litany of white-collar crimes. Balwani was separately convicted in 12 felony counts of fraud and conspiracy and sentenced to nearly 13 years in a Southern California prison. The filmmakers more than once asked the Alice Tully Hall crowd to preserve the surprise twists and turns the movie takes as it shifts. That includes dramatic recreations with the aid of an A-list star and other elaborations, all in an effort to get closer to the truth. But even as Fielder and Oppenheimer pleaded for viewers not to discuss the film in too much detail, they were clearly eager to debate and try to make sense of “You Can See Everything.” “As each scene that happens, it’s happening and we’re documenting it. There’s no plan of what’s going to happen next at any point,” Fielder said. “This is a path that opened up to us and we just followed it.”

headlines.title: Oakland's Skyline High cancels remainder of varsity football season
headlines.description: Oakland’s Skyline High School is reportedly canceling the remainder of its varsity football season because of a lack of players and safety concerns. According to the East Bay Times, the school’s principal sent an email indicating the team does not have the required number of players because of injuries, transfers and other issues. The shortage led to safety concerns and prompted the decision to cancel the remainder of the season. Skyline had already forfeited its previous three games for the same reasons. Other Bay Area high schools have made similar moves this fall, including Richmond and Mount Diablo.

headlines.title: SF lifts shelter-in-place, evacuations after underground vault eruptions
headlines.description: A shelter-in-place order and evacuations were lifted Thursday after four underground vaults erupted in downtown San Francisco, according to the fire department. Firefighters responded around 6:04 a.m. to the 100 to 200 block of California Street following reports of smoke coming from several street-side underground vaults. Four vaults experienced eruptions that were isolated to the vaults, SFFD said. “We did not put eyes on fire,” SFFD Lt. Bruno Bovo said. “There was a couple reactions from one of the vaults, which we are calling eruptions, approximately 10 minutes apart. It was a fireball that came from one of the vaults.” PG&E said it experienced what it called an underground incident involving a low-voltage cable. “The low-voltage cable experienced an issue,” PG&E spokesperson Tamar Sarkissian said. “When we got out here, there was smoldering. We actually adjusted the vault lid to allow for that smoldering to vent. The vault lids never came undone, they didn’t dislodge. We actually have safety equipment in place to prevent that from happening.” A unified command was established with the police and fire departments as well as PG&E. The immediate area was evacuated and the surrounding area also was cordoned off. There were shelter-in-place orders in the 100 to 300 blocks of California and Front streets until around 10 a.m. PG&E shut down additional power, which affected more locations in the area. Power has since been restored to all but one affected customer, the utility said. No injuries were reported. The fire department and PG&E are investigating the cause of the fire.

headlines.title: 3 indicted in kidnapping, killing of Tracy man
headlines.description: Three people who remain at large have been indicted in connection with the February kidnapping and killing of a Tracy man who investigators determined was not the intended target, the San Joaquin County Sheriff’s Office said. Avtar Singh, 57, was kidnapped Feb. 17 from the Gurdwara Gur Nanak Parkash in Tracy. Surveillance video showed a white SUV and three people dressed in dark clothing apparently forcing Singh into the vehicle. Singh’s body was found days later in a remote area near Lake Berryessa. The Napa County Sheriff’s Office located his body on Feb. 20. Singh was survived by his wife and 6-month-old triplets. Investigators later determined that he was not the intended target, the San Joaquin County Sheriff’s Office said in a statement Wednesday. The people indicted are Alberto Alonso Alencastro, 25; Alfonso Cresencio Segura Arellano, 20; and Barnabe Antonio Segura Arellano, 22. (L-R) Alberto Alencastro, Alfonso Segura, and Barnabe Segura. (San Joaquin County Sheriff’s Office) All three remain at large. Authorities are asking anyone who recognizes them, knows their whereabouts, or has information that could help investigators to contact the San Joaquin County Sheriff’s Office. Authorities warned people not to approach or try to apprehend the three.

headlines.title: Former airline pilot, girlfriend convicted of child sex abuse, East Bay DA says
headlines.description: A former airline pilot and his girlfriend were convicted of child sexual abuse, the Contra Costa County District Attorney’s Office said Wednesday. Florida resident Rustom Bhagwagar, 35, a former pilot for Delta Airlines, was arrested at the San Francisco International Airport in July 2025 by the Contra Costa County Sheriff’s Office and was held on $15 million bail. He was charged with 24 felonies related to the repeated sex abuse of a young girl. The criminal case against Bhagwagar and co-defendant and Walnut Creek resident Jennifer Spitz Powell, 46, was handled by two separate juries, prosecutors said. A jury found Powell guilty on Monday, and another jury found Bhagwagar guilty on Tuesday. Both were convicted of eight counts of sex abuse on a child under 10 years of age and 12 counts of forcible lewd acts upon a child under the age of 14. Evidence presented to both juries showed that the sexual abuse of the victim began when she was 7 years old and occurred from 2017 to 2022. Powell, who was in a relationship with Bhagwagar, participated with him in numerous acts of abuse against the victim, according to prosecutors. Bhagwagar and Powell each face a maximum sentence of 230 years to life in state prison and will be sentenced at a future date, the district attorney’s office said. “This young survivor showed extraordinary courage by testifying in court and facing the people who used duress to harm her,” said District Attorney Diana Becton in a statement released by her office. “These verdicts hold both defendants accountable.”
headlines.source: Katy St. Clair | Bay City News

headlines.title: Valkyries fans remain optimistic heading into playoff game 3 against Dallas
headlines.description: Fans of the Golden State Valkyries said they remain optimistic — despite the team’s loss in game 2 of the first round of the WNBA playoffs to the Dallas Wings — that their team will prevail in this postseason run. While the Valkyries were in Dallas Wednesday playing at the home of the Wings, Bay Area fans headed to watch parties locally to tune in to the game. Likely the largest watch party was the official, free watch party on the big screen at Thrive City just outside Chase Center. This time, Valkyries fans added a new tradition. Borrowing from the success of pre-watch party marches up to Thrive City during World Cup matches, Valkyries fans marched by the hundreds up the block ahead of Wednesday’s game. They were led by the Valkyries’ mascot, Violet, and Oakland’s Fremont High School marching band. Fans stayed in Thrive City watching the game as it stretched into overtime, cycling back between elation and disappointment as the teams traded off taking the lead in the game. Ultimately, the Wings bested the Valkyries 108 to 100. With the series now tied at 1-1, the teams will next face off on Friday, October 2, at the Valkyries home at Chase Center. Valkyries fans on Wednesday said they are feeling optimistic that the Valkyries will have a home-court advantage with the fan energy at Ballhalla on Friday. Many fans said they believe the Valkyries could make it all the way this year in the playoffs. “I’m feeling pretty confident that they’re going to pull it off, hopefully they’ll go to the very end and win,” said Judy Bacchus of Hayward. The Valkyries are in their second season as a team and in their second postseason run. Fans said the energy and confidence this postseason feels particularly high. “It’s so wonderful that San Francisco got a women’s basketball team, and I think that we here in the Bay Area want to support that,” Bacchus said. “And the fans have proven that, coming out, selling out the arena every game, so I want to be a part of that,” she continued.

headlines.title: Ogunbowale scores WNBA playoff-record 45 as Wings win in OT to force deciding game with Valkyries
headlines.description: Arike Ogunbowale scored a WNBA playoff-record 45 points, including a tying 3-pointer in the final seconds of regulation, and the Dallas Wings beat the Golden State Valkyries 108-100 in an overtime thriller Wednesday night, forcing a deciding Game 3 in their first-round series. Ogunbowale opened the extra period by banking in a 3, then hit another one to put Dallas ahead for good at 103-100 with 1:46 remaining. She easily topped her previous playoff best of 24 points. The four-time All-Star’s off-balance corner 3 for a 93-93 tie with 4.1 seconds left in Game 2 was followed by Gabby Williams getting called for an offensive foul on the inbound play after a Golden State timeout. That call was reversed on replay, so instead of Aziaha James having a chance to give Dallas the lead at the free-throw line, there was a jump ball at center court with 3.0 seconds to go. After a scramble for the loose ball, Golden State’s desperation shot was way off target, and after the buzzer. The deciding game will be Friday night in San Francisco, where the Valkyries won the series opener by 24 points. Golden State is looking to advance in the playoffs for the first time in the franchise’s second season. The late drama overshadowed an off night for Wings star Paige Bueckers, who is making her postseason debut. The 2025 No. 1 overall pick and Rookie of the Year scored 10 points on 3-of-13 shooting. Williams scored a career-high 36 points, regular season or playoffs, but missed all six of her shots in the final 1:31 of overtime to finish 12 of 23 from the field. Dallas’ Alysha Clark tied her playoff career high with 21 points. ___ See AP’s full WNBA coverage here
